These are edited excerpts from my analysis notebook. I have retained the
processing sequence and ordinary analysis settings, while removing project
identifiers, marker panels, recorded outputs, and interpretations.
No count matrices or research results are included.

The excerpts have not been rerun: the required inputs are private. Chunks are
disabled for knitting so that the public notebook displays code only. To use
them locally, supply the inputs below and run the relevant chunks in order.
The retained QC thresholds, number of PCs, and clustering resolution require
review for the dataset being analysed; they are not universal defaults.

```{r setup, include=FALSE, eval=TRUE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, echo = TRUE)
```

## Libraries and local inputs

Use Seurat v5 for the `JoinLayers` block. The private sample manifest has columns
`sample_id` and `relative_counts_dir`: the latter identifies a corrected matrix
folder relative to `data/private/`. The manifest itself is not distributed.
Each sample ID must identify an independent capture for the doublet step.

```{r libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(Seurat)
library(patchwork)
library(ggplot2)
library(sctransform)
library(scDblFinder)
library(DropletUtils)
library(SoupX)
library(Matrix)

set.seed(1234)
input_root <- "data/private"
output_root <- "outputs/private"
dir.create(output_root, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

colors <- c('#1f77b4', '#ff7f0e', '#279e68', '#d62728', '#aa40fc', '#8c564b',
            '#e377c2', '#b5bd61', '#17becf', '#aec7e8', '#ffbb78', '#98df8a',
            '#ff9896', '#c5b0d5', '#c49c94', '#f7b6d2', '#dbdb8d', '#9edae5',
            '#ad494a', '#8c6d31', '#FF34FF', '#763568', '#63FFAC', '#B79762',
            '#004D43', '#002dff', '#997D87', '#5A0007', '#809693', '#6A3A4C',
            '#1B4400', '#4FC601', '#3B5DFF', '#4A3B53', '#FF2F80', '#61615A',
            '#BA0900', '#6B7900', '#00C2A0', '#FFAA92', '#FF90C9', '#B903AA',
            '#D16100', '#DDEFFF', '#000035', '#7B4F4B', '#A1C299', '#300018',
            '#0AA6D8', '#013349', '#00846F', '#372101', '#FFB500', '#C2FFED',
            '#A079BF', '#CC0744', 'yellow', 'green', 'magenta', 'red')
```

## SoupX for one capture

The raw matrix includes background droplets; the filtered matrix contains the
cell-containing droplets from the same capture. Repeat this block per capture
before building the corrected-matrix manifest. Input and output folder names
below are placeholders.

```{r load-counts}
raw_matrix <- Read10X(data.dir = file.path(input_root, "capture", "raw_feature_bc_matrix"))
filt_matrix <- Read10X(data.dir = file.path(input_root, "capture", "filtered_feature_bc_matrix"))
stopifnot(identical(rownames(raw_matrix), rownames(filt_matrix)))
stopifnot(all(colnames(filt_matrix) %in% colnames(raw_matrix)))

# Create soup channel.
sc <- SoupChannel(raw_matrix, filt_matrix)

# Cluster the filtered object before contamination estimation.
capture_obj <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = filt_matrix)
capture_obj <- NormalizeData(capture_obj)
capture_obj <- FindVariableFeatures(capture_obj)
capture_obj <- ScaleData(capture_obj)
capture_obj <- RunPCA(capture_obj)
capture_obj <- FindNeighbors(capture_obj)
capture_obj <- FindClusters(capture_obj, resolution = 0.5)

clusters <- capture_obj@meta.data$seurat_clusters
# Editorial cleanup: attach barcode names explicitly.
names(clusters) <- colnames(capture_obj)
sc <- setClusters(sc, clusters)

# Estimate contamination and adjust the matrix.
sc <- autoEstCont(sc)
adj_matrix <- adjustCounts(sc)

# Editorial cleanup: use the exported DropletUtils interface.
DropletUtils::write10xCounts(
  file.path(output_root, "corrected_capture"), adj_matrix
)
```

`autoEstCont` requires appropriate expression structure and background droplets.
An estimation failure should be investigated rather than replaced by an
unreported fixed contamination fraction. Corrected matrices are local outputs.

## Combine corrected matrices

Place the corrected-matrix folders under `data/private/` before listing them in
the manifest. Each manifest row supplies the relative folder and capture ID.

```{r combine-captures}
sample_manifest <- read.csv(file.path(input_root, "sample_manifest.csv"),
                            stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
stopifnot(all(c("sample_id", "relative_counts_dir") %in% names(sample_manifest)))
stopifnot(nrow(sample_manifest) > 0, !anyDuplicated(sample_manifest$sample_id))
data_paths <- file.path(input_root, sample_manifest$relative_counts_dir)
sample_names <- sample_manifest$sample_id

seurat_list <- list()
for (i in seq_along(data_paths)) {
  mtx <- Read10X(data.dir = data_paths[[i]])
  seu <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = mtx, project = sample_names[[i]],
                            min.cells = 30, min.features = 200)
  # Editorial cleanup: store capture identity before merging.
  seu$Samples <- sample_names[[i]]
  seurat_list[[i]] <- seu
}

if (length(seurat_list) > 1) {
  merged_seurat <- merge(seurat_list[[1]], y = seurat_list[-1],
                         add.cell.ids = sample_names, project = "CorrectedCounts")
} else {
  merged_seurat <- seurat_list[[1]]
}
merged_seurat[["RNA"]] <- JoinLayers(merged_seurat[["RNA"]])
```

The manifest replaces the original sample list. Barcode prefixes and the
`Samples` column replace the original sample-label reconstruction after merging.
No sample identities, number of captures, or group assignments are encoded here.

## QC and a preliminary embedding

The two prefixes in the mitochondrial expression pattern accommodate common
gene-name conventions; check that the pattern matches the intended annotation.
The notebook's feature-count and percentage thresholds are retained as code
settings, without the original cell counts or decisions based on those counts.

```{r quality-control}
merged_seurat[["percent.mt"]] <- PercentageFeatureSet(
  merged_seurat, pattern = "^MT-|^mt-"
)
VlnPlot(merged_seurat, features = c("nFeature_RNA", "nCount_RNA", "percent.mt"),
        group.by = "Samples", ncol = 3, pt.size = 0)

analysis_obj <- subset(merged_seurat,
  subset = nFeature_RNA > 200 & nFeature_RNA < 10000 & percent.mt < 10
)
analysis_obj <- NormalizeData(analysis_obj)
analysis_obj <- FindVariableFeatures(analysis_obj, selection.method = "vst", nfeatures = 2000)
analysis_obj <- ScaleData(analysis_obj)
analysis_obj <- RunPCA(analysis_obj, npcs = 100)
ElbowPlot(analysis_obj, ndims = 50)

# One of the dimensionality choices explored in the source notebook.
# Review dimensionality and resolution for a new dataset before using them.
analysis_obj <- FindNeighbors(analysis_obj, dims = 1:15, verbose = FALSE)
analysis_obj <- FindClusters(analysis_obj, verbose = FALSE, resolution = 0.5)
analysis_obj <- RunUMAP(analysis_obj, dims = 1:15, verbose = FALSE)
DimPlot(analysis_obj, label = TRUE, reduction = "umap", cols = colors, pt.size = 0.2)
DimPlot(analysis_obj, reduction = "umap", cols = colors,
        group.by = "Samples", pt.size = 0.2)
```

This excerpt assumes enough cells and variable features for the requested PCs.
The original separate feature-removal and biological cluster-cleanup decisions
are omitted. The embedding above is for doublet review; it should be recomputed
after filtering if used for downstream interpretation.

## scDblFinder by capture

The sample argument defines independent captures. `clusters = TRUE` requests
clustering within the doublet workflow; it does not supply biological labels.

```{r doublet-review}
# Proxy object and conversion to SingleCellExperiment.
checkdb <- analysis_obj
rna <- as.SingleCellExperiment(x = checkdb, assay = "RNA")
xtc <- scDblFinder(rna, samples = "Samples", clusters = TRUE)

# Editorial cleanup: use the public accessor and align calls by barcode.
doublet_calls <- data.frame(doublet = xtc$scDblFinder.class,
                            row.names = colnames(xtc))
analysis_obj$dbr <- doublet_calls[colnames(analysis_obj), "doublet"]
analysis_obj@meta.data <- analysis_obj@meta.data %>%
  dplyr::rename(scDBLFinder = dbr)
analysis_obj$scDBLFinder <- factor(analysis_obj$scDBLFinder,
                                  levels = c("doublet", "singlet"))

table(analysis_obj$scDBLFinder)
DimPlot(analysis_obj, reduction = "umap", group.by = "scDBLFinder",
        cols = colors, label = TRUE, pt.size = 0.01)

Idents(analysis_obj) <- "scDBLFinder"
singlets <- subset(analysis_obj, idents = "singlet")
saveRDS(singlets, file = file.path(output_root, "singlets.rds"))
```

No doublet counts, fitted contamination estimates, or plotted outputs are
included. The exploratory DoubletFinder branch and its manually selected
parameters are omitted. Normalization, PCA, clustering, and UMAP need to be
revisited on the retained cells before broad annotation.

```{r record-environment}
capture.output(sessionInfo(), file = file.path(output_root, "sessionInfo.txt"))
```
